description: Secure-channel conformance vectors for protocol version 1: the handshake, key schedule and sealing of spec/secure-channel.cddl, on real key material that is made up for these vectors and is test material only. The top-level vectors are every hello and every sealed secure-data frame, round-tripped like any other vector file. The secure_channel section adds what a round trip cannot: for each handshake the fixed ephemeral keys and nonces, each hello's signing input and signature, the shared secret, salt, HKDF info and both direction keys, and a transcript of sealed frames with each IV, associated data and ciphertext; the verdict a receiver gives for each hello (ok, or the reason it is refused: wrong_recipient, unsupported_identity_alg, invalid_identity_key or bad_signature, checked in the order the spec states); the establish verdicts for ephemeral keys that cannot be used; and sequences of secure-data frames to open in order, each step with the result a conformant channel must give (an opened frame, replayed, unauthentic or undecodable), including counters up to 2^64 - 1 that a narrower implementation must refuse and not truncate. Every key and identity in the file is made up for it and marked synthetic. Ed25519 signatures and AES-GCM are deterministic, so regenerating reproduces them byte for byte. ES256 signatures are not: such a hello is verify-only, its signature is emitted once and kept on regeneration while its signing input is unchanged, and an implementation checks it verifies and never expects to reproduce it.
